attributes.description: Deadline by which the athlete must respond to a missed or incomplete filing notification. Typically 14 days from notification_date per WADA ISTI. Failure to respond within this window may result in the missed filing being confirmed.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.4

attributes.name: authorised_representative_name
attributes.description: Full name of the authorised representative (agent, coach, or team official) who submitted the filing on behalf of the athlete, where applicable. Null if the athlete submitted directly.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.2

attributes.name: cas_case_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) Case Reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the CAS arbitration case associated with a disputed whereabouts filing violation, if applicable. Null if no CAS proceedings have been initiated. Format follows CAS standard case numbering (e.g., CAS 2024/A/9876).
attributes.references: CAS Arbitration Rules; WADA Code Article 13

attributes.name: competition_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the scheduled competition or event during the filing period. Defines the in-competition period boundary for testing jurisdiction and sample classification purposes.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(d)

attributes.name: competition_location
attributes.description: City and country of the competition venue where the athlete is scheduled to compete during the filing period. Supports in-competition testing logistics and jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(d)

attributes.name: competition_name
attributes.description: Name of any competition or event the athlete is scheduled to participate in during the filing period. Required to enable in-competition testing planning and to distinguish in-competition from out-of-competition samples.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(d)

attributes.name: competition_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the scheduled competition or event during the filing period. Used to plan in-competition doping control and to validate athlete availability windows.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(d)

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Regulatory compliance determination for this filing period. COMPLIANT = filed on time and complete; MISSED = not filed by deadline; INCOMPLETE = filed but missing required information; LATE = filed after deadline; UNDER_REVIEW = compliance determination pending adjudication. Three MISSED or INCOMPLETE filings within 12 months trigger a WADA Code Article 2.4 violation.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 2.4; WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this whereabouts filing record was first created in the compliance data platform. Provides the audit trail creation anchor for the Silver Layer lakehouse record.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; WADA ISTI Article 11

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Origin system or ingestion method through which this whereabouts filing record was loaded into the compliance data platform. ADAMS = direct integration with WADA ADAMS portal; MANUAL_ENTRY = entered by compliance staff; API_INTEGRATION = via anti-doping organisation API; BULK_IMPORT = batch file load.
attributes.references: WADA ADAMS System; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason provided by the athlete or their representative for disputing a missed or incomplete filing determination. Relevant for CAS arbitration proceedings and WADA Code Article 2.4 adjudication.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 2.4; CAS Arbitration Rules

attributes.name: filing_deadline
attributes.description: Regulatory deadline by which the athlete must submit their whereabouts filing for the applicable quarter. Typically the last day of the preceding quarter per WADA ISTI requirements.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.1

attributes.name: filing_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments recorded by the compliance officer or anti-doping administrator regarding this whereabouts filing. May include exceptional circumstances, force majeure events, or administrative observations relevant to compliance adjudication.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11; ISO 20121 Event Sustainability Management

attributes.name: filing_period_quarter
attributes.description: Calendar quarter (1=Q1 Jan-Mar, 2=Q2 Apr-Jun, 3=Q3 Jul-Sep, 4=Q4 Oct-Dec) to which this whereabouts filing applies. Under WADA Code Article 2.4, three missed filings within 12 months constitute a whereabouts failure violation.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.1; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: filing_period_year
attributes.description: Calendar year (e.g., 2024) to which this whereabouts filing applies. Combined with filing_period_quarter to uniquely identify the quarterly filing obligation period.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.1

attributes.name: is_late_submission
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the filing was submitted after the regulatory deadline (submission_date > filing_deadline). Late submissions may be treated as incomplete or missed filings depending on the anti-doping organisation's rules.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the most recent amendment or update to this whereabouts filing record. Supports audit trail requirements and compliance adjudication when disputes arise over filing completeness.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: missed_filing_count_rolling_12m
attributes.description: Running count of missed or non-compliant whereabouts filings by this athlete within the preceding 12-month rolling window at the time of this filing. When this value reaches 3, a WADA Code Article 2.4 whereabouts failure violation is triggered. Stored as a point-in-time snapshot for audit and adjudication purposes.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 2.4; WADA ISTI Article 11.3.4

attributes.name: notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the athlete was formally notified of the missed or incomplete filing determination. The 14-day response window for the athlete to contest the determination begins from this date.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.4; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: notification_sent
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the athlete has been formally notified of a missed or incomplete filing determination as required by WADA ISTI. Notification is a prerequisite before a missed filing can be counted toward the Article 2.4 violation threshold.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.4; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: overnight_location_address
attributes.description: Full street address where the athlete will be sleeping each night during the filing period. Required field under WADA ISTI for out-of-competition testing. Classified as restricted PII as it reveals the athlete's residential or accommodation location.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(a)

attributes.name: overnight_location_city
attributes.description: City component of the athlete's overnight location for the filing period. Supports geographic analysis of testing pool distribution and logistics planning for out-of-competition testing.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(a)

attributes.name: overnight_location_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the athlete's overnight location during the filing period. Used to coordinate testing jurisdiction between national and international anti-doping organisations.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(a); ISO 3166-1

attributes.name: responsible_organisation
attributes.description: Name of the Anti-Doping Organisation (ADO) responsible for managing this athlete's whereabouts filing obligation for the period (e.g., WADA, USADA, UKAD, or the relevant International Federation). Determines which body adjudicates missed filing violations.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.2.1; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the compliance review process for this filing. PENDING = awaiting review; IN_REVIEW = under active compliance review; ACCEPTED = compliance determination finalised; DISPUTED = athlete or representative has contested the compliance determination; ESCALATED = referred to CAS or governing body for adjudication.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 2.4; CAS Arbitration Rules; WADA ISTI Article 11.3.4

attributes.name: sixty_minute_slot_time
attributes.description: Specific 60-minute daily time window (HH:MM in 24-hour format, representing start of slot) during which the athlete guarantees availability for out-of-competition testing at the declared training venue. This is a mandatory WADA ISTI requirement for Registered Testing Pool athletes.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(c)

attributes.name: sport_discipline
attributes.description: Sport and discipline for which the athlete is registered in the testing pool (e.g., Athletics - 100m Sprint, Swimming - Freestyle, Football). Used for sport-specific whereabouts rule application and reporting to governing bodies such as FIFA, IOC, or relevant International Federation.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.2; IOC Anti-Doping Rules

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the athlete or their authorised representative submitted the whereabouts filing. Used to determine whether the filing was on-time or late relative to the filing_deadline.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.2

attributes.name: submission_method
attributes.description: Channel or mechanism through which the whereabouts filing was submitted. ADAMS_PORTAL and ADAMS_MOBILE are the primary WADA-approved electronic submission methods. Other methods may be accepted in exceptional circumstances per anti-doping organisation policy.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.2

attributes.name: submission_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the whereabouts filing was received and recorded in the ADAMS portal. Provides audit-grade precision for compliance adjudication.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.2; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: submitted_by
attributes.description: Role of the person who submitted the whereabouts filing on behalf of the athlete. Athletes may authorise agents, coaches, or team officials to submit on their behalf via ADAMS. Relevant for accountability and adjudication of missed filing disputes.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.2; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: testing_pool_type
attributes.description: Classification of the registered testing pool to which the athlete belongs. RTP = Registered Testing Pool (international-level, managed by International Federation or WADA); NRTP = National Registered Testing Pool (managed by National Anti-Doping Organisation); TP = Testing Pool (lower-tier, no whereabouts filing obligation but tracked for completeness).
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.2; WADA Code Article 2.4

attributes.name: training_schedule_end_time
attributes.description: Scheduled end time of the athlete's regular training sessions during the filing period. Together with training_schedule_start_time, defines the daily availability window for doping control officers.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(b)

attributes.name: training_schedule_start_time
attributes.description: Scheduled start time of the athlete's regular training sessions during the filing period. Combined with training_schedule_end_time, defines the 60-minute testing slot window required by WADA ISTI.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(b)

attributes.name: training_venue_address
attributes.description: Full street address of the primary training venue for the filing period. Enables doping control officers to locate the athlete for unannounced out-of-competition testing.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(b)

attributes.name: training_venue_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary training facility or venue where the athlete trains during the filing period. Required for out-of-competition testing planning and sample collection logistics.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3(b)

attributes.name: update_count
attributes.description: Number of times this whereabouts filing has been updated or amended after initial submission. Athletes may update filings up to the deadline without penalty; updates after the deadline may be flagged for review.
attributes.references: WADA ISTI Article 11.3.3

attributes.name: violation_threshold_reached
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this filing caused the athlete's missed filing count to reach or exceed the WADA Code Article 2.4 threshold of three missed/incomplete filings within 12 months, triggering a formal whereabouts failure violation.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 2.4

products.name: eligibility_certification
products.description: Unified eligibility, certification, and exemption record confirming or modifying compliance status for athletes, participants, venues, and events. For certifications: covers league eligibility, amateur status, age/nationality eligibility, anti-doping clearance, medical clearance, ADA venue accessibility certification, and event safety certification. For exemptions: covers Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUEs per WADA Code Article 4.4), broadcast territorial exemptions, ADA undue hardship exemptions, and FCC content exemptions. Captures record type (certification/exemption), issuing or reviewing authority, certified/exempt entity, effective and expiry dates, status, conditions or restrictions, medical justification (for TUEs), approved substance/method, WADA ADAMS TUE reference, and accommodation requirements. Integrates with athlete domain for competition gating and venue domain for operational permits.

attributes.name: eligibility_certification_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each eligibility certification or exemption record within the compliance domain. Primary key for this data product.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard

The eligibility_certification has cas_case_reference as a string field. Replacing this with a FK to ar

attributes.name: athlete_athlete_profile_id

attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; CAS Procedural Rules

attributes.name: athlete_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the athlete profile when the certified or exempt entity is an individual athlete or participant. Null when the record pertains to a venue or event.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; CAS Procedural Rules

attributes.name: event_fixture_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific event or fixture for which this certification or exemption applies. Null when the record is entity-level rather than event-specific.
attributes.references: FIFA Regulations; NFL Governance Office; NBA League Office

attributes.name: exemption_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.exemption. Business justification: An eligibility certification may be granted specifically because of a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE). The eligibility_certification has wada_adams_tue_reference as a string field; replacing this with
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: fixture_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific event or fixture for which this certification or exemption applies. Null when the record is entity-level rather than event-specific.
attributes.references: FIFA Regulations; NFL Governance Office; NBA League Office

attributes.name: litigation_case_id

attributes.name: sanction_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sanction. Business justification: An eligibility certification may be directly affected by a sanction (e.g., a ban that modifies competition eligibility). Linking eligibility_certification to the sanction that triggered the eligibilit
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: staff_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the venue when the certified or exempt entity is a facility (e.g., ADA accessibility certification, event safety permit). Null when the record pertains to an athlete.
attributes.references: ADA Title III; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; ISO 20121

attributes.name: venue_id
attributes.description: Reference to the venue when the certified or exempt entity is a facility (e.g., ADA accessibility certification, event safety permit). Null when the record pertains to an athlete.
attributes.references: ADA Title III; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; ISO 20121

attributes.name: ada_accommodation_requirements
attributes.business_glossary_term: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodation Requirements
attributes.description: Detailed description of specific accessibility accommodations required or certified under ADA Title III for venue certifications or ADA undue hardship exemptions. Includes wheelchair access, assistive listening systems, accessible seating, and service animal provisions. Null for non-ADA certification types.
attributes.references: ADA Title III; ADA Standards for Accessible Design; DOJ ADA Regulations 28 CFR Part 36

attributes.name: age_eligibility_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the athlete's age has been formally verified against the applicable league or competition minimum/maximum age requirements (True = verified and compliant; False = not yet verified or non-compliant). Relevant for draft eligibility, youth competition, and veteran status certifications.
attributes.references: NBA Draft Eligibility Rules; NFL Draft Eligibility Rules; FIFA Youth Competition Regulations; IOC Age Eligibility Rules

attributes.name: appeal_status
attributes.description: Current status of any appeal filed against a denial or revocation decision for this certification or exemption. Tracks the appeal lifecycle from filing through CAS or internal arbitration resolution.
attributes.references: CAS Code of Sports-related Arbitration; WADA Code Article 13; FIFA Disciplinary Code; ADA Administrative Appeal Process

attributes.name: application_date
attributes.description: Date on which the certification or exemption application was formally submitted to the issuing authority. Used for SLA tracking, regulatory deadline compliance, and audit trail.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4 (TUE retroactive application rules); FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: approved_substance
attributes.description: Name of the specific prohibited substance or method for which a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) has been granted under WADA Code Article 4.4. Null for non-TUE certification types. Must reference the WADA Prohibited List substance name.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; WADA Prohibited List (annually updated); WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE)

attributes.name: broadcast_territory_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country or territory code for which a broadcast territorial exemption applies. Used for FCC content exemptions and RSN blackout rule overrides. Null for non-broadcast exemption types.
attributes.references: FCC Broadcast Regulations; RSN Territorial Rights Agreements; FIFA Media Rights Regulations

attributes.name: cba_provision_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) article or provision that governs this eligibility certification (e.g., drug testing protocols, medical clearance requirements, grievance procedures). Null when CBA is not applicable.
attributes.references: NFL CBA; NBA CBA; MLB CBA; NHL CBA; MLS CBA

attributes.name: certification_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference number assigned by the issuing authority (e.g., WADA ADAMS TUE reference, ADA compliance certificate number, league eligibility certificate number). Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory correspondence.
attributes.references: WADA ADAMS System; ADA Title III; FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: certification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the certification or exemption record. Drives competition gating for athletes and operational permit status for venues. 'Pending' indicates under review; 'Approved' confirms active compliance; 'Denied' records rejection; 'Suspended' indicates temporary hold; 'Revoked' indicates withdrawal; 'Expired' indicates lapse past effective period.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Title III; FIFA Eligibility Regulations; NBA/NFL/MLB/NHL Governance Rules

attributes.name: certification_type
attributes.description: Specific category of certification or exemption. Examples include: league_eligibility, amateur_status, age_nationality_eligibility, anti_doping_clearance, medical_clearance, ada_venue_accessibility, event_safety, therapeutic_use_exemption (TUE), broadcast_territorial_exemption, ada_undue_hardship, fcc_content_exemption. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: league_eligibility|amateur_status|age_nationality_eligibility|anti_doping_clearance|medical_clearance|ada_venue_accessibility|event_safety|therapeutic_use_exemption|broadcast_territorial_exemption|ada_undue_hardship|fcc_content_exemption — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Title III; FCC Broadcast Regulations; FIFA Eligibility Regulations; NBA/NFL/MLB/NHL/MLS Governance Rules

attributes.name: certified_entity_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the certified or exempt entity (athlete full name, venue name, event name, or organization name) at the time of certification issuance. Preserved for audit and historical reporting independent of master record changes.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Accuracy); SOX Section 302

attributes.name: certified_entity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the entity to which this certification or exemption applies. Determines which domain FK (athlete_id, venue_id, event_id) is populated and governs applicable regulatory framework.
attributes.references: WADA Code; ADA Title III; ISO 20121; FIFA Regulations

attributes.name: competition_eligibility_flag
attributes.description: Derived operational flag indicating whether the certified entity is currently cleared for competition or operational use based on the current certification status and effective/expiry dates. True = eligible; False = ineligible. Used as the primary gate in athlete rostering and event participation systems.
attributes.references: NFL/NBA/MLB/NHL/MLS Eligibility Rules; FIFA Eligibility Regulations; WADA Code

attributes.name: compliance_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory or governance framework under which this certification or exemption is issued. Enables framework-specific reporting, audit scheduling, and policy enforcement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WADA|ADA|FCC|GDPR|CCPA|PCI_DSS|OSHA|FIFA|IOC|CBA|SOX|ISO_20121 — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: WADA Code; ADA Title III; FCC Rules; GDPR; CCPA; PCI-DSS; OSHA; FIFA Statutes; IOC Charter; SOX; ISO 20121

attributes.name: conditions_restrictions
attributes.description: Free-text description of any conditions, limitations, or restrictions attached to this certification or exemption (e.g., 'valid only for regular season competition', 'subject to quarterly medical review', 'restricted to home venue only'). Null if unconditional.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Reasonable Accommodation Standard; FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this eligibility certification record was first created in the compliance system. Serves as the authoritative audit creation marker per SOX and GDPR accountability requirements.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5 (Accountability); ISO 20121

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date on which the issuing authority rendered its decision (approval, denial, or conditional approval) on the certification or exemption application. Used for regulatory SLA compliance measurement.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; CAS Procedural Rules; ADA Title III

attributes.name: denial_reason
attributes.description: Structured reason code or free-text explanation provided by the issuing authority when a certification or exemption application is denied or revoked. Required for appeal processes and regulatory audit trails. Null when status is not denied or revoked.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; CAS Procedural Rules; ADA Title III; FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which this certification or exemption becomes legally binding and operationally active. Used for competition eligibility gating and venue operational permit activation.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Title III; FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which this certification or exemption ceases to be valid. Null for open-ended certifications. Triggers renewal workflow and competition eligibility suspension if not renewed prior to this date.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Title III; FIFA Eligibility Regulations; OSHA Permit Requirements

attributes.name: governing_body_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the primary governing body whose regulations this certification or exemption satisfies. Enables multi-regulatory reporting and compliance dashboard segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WADA|FIFA|IOC|NFL|NBA|MLB|NHL|MLS|FCC|ADA|OSHA|CAS|SEC|SOX|GDPR|CCPA|PCI_SSC — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FIFA Statutes; IOC Charter; NFL/NBA/MLB/NHL/MLS Governance Rules; FCC Rules; WADA Code; ADA; OSHA; CAS Code

attributes.name: is_retroactive
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification or exemption was granted retroactively (True) or prospectively (False). Particularly relevant for WADA Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUEs) where retroactive approval is permitted under specific circumstances per WADA Code Article 4.4.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4 (Retroactive TUE); FIFA Eligibility Regulations

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the governing body, regulatory agency, or internal compliance function that issued or approved this certification or exemption (e.g., WADA, FIFA, NFL League Office, ADA Compliance Office, FCC, CAS, OSHA). Critical for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: WADA Code; FIFA Statutes; ADA Title III; FCC Rules; OSHA 29 CFR; CAS Code of Sports-related Arbitration

attributes.name: issuing_authority_reference
attributes.description: Official reference number, case number, or docket identifier assigned by the issuing authority for this certification or exemption (e.g., WADA ADAMS TUE reference ID, CAS case number, FCC docket number). Enables direct cross-referencing with external regulatory systems.
attributes.references: WADA ADAMS; CAS Procedural Rules; FCC Electronic Comment Filing System

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this eligibility certification record. Used for change tracking, audit trail completeness, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5 (Accountability); ISO 20121

attributes.name: league_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the specific professional league or competition structure to which this certification applies (e.g., NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS, UEFA_CL). Scopes the eligibility certification to the correct competition jurisdiction.
attributes.references: NFL Governance Office; NBA League Office; MLB Commissioner's Office; NHL Board of Governors; MLS Rules

attributes.name: medical_justification
attributes.description: Clinical rationale and medical necessity statement supporting a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) or medical clearance certification. Documents the diagnosed condition, treatment necessity, and absence of performance-enhancing effect. Classified confidential due to sensitive health information context at the organizational compliance level.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE); GDPR Article 9 (Special Category Health Data); HIPAA (where applicable)

attributes.name: nationality_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the nationality or federation affiliation relevant to this eligibility certification (e.g., USA, GBR, BRA). Used for age/nationality eligibility certifications and international cap tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; FIFA Eligibility Regulations Article 5; IOC Eligibility Rules

attributes.name: prohibited_list_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the WADA Prohibited List in effect at the time of TUE application or anti-doping clearance certification (format: YYYY-MM, e.g., 2024-01). Ensures traceability to the correct annual prohibited substance list. Null for non-anti-doping certification types.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.1; WADA Prohibited List (annually updated January 1)

attributes.name: record_type
attributes.description: Discriminator indicating whether this record represents a positive certification (confirming compliance status) or an exemption (granting relief from a standard requirement). Drives downstream processing logic and reporting segmentation.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; ADA Undue Hardship Standard; FCC Content Exemption Rules

attributes.name: renewal_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which a renewal application must be submitted to maintain continuous certification or exemption coverage. Typically set prior to expiry_date to allow processing time. Null when renewal_required is False.
attributes.references: WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE); ADA Title III; OSHA Permit Renewal Requirements

attributes.name: renewal_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this certification or exemption requires periodic renewal (True) or is granted on a permanent basis (False). Drives automated renewal reminder workflows and compliance calendar scheduling.
attributes.references: WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE); ADA Title III; OSHA Permit Renewal Requirements

attributes.name: reviewing_officer
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the compliance officer, medical officer, or regulatory representative responsible for reviewing and processing this certification or exemption application within the organization. Used for internal accountability and audit trail.
attributes.references: SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5 (Accountability); ISO 20121

attributes.name: season_year
attributes.description: Four-digit calendar year representing the competitive season for which this certification is valid (e.g., 2024 for the 2024-25 season). Used for season-scoped eligibility gating and annual compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NFL/NBA/MLB/NHL/MLS Season Governance Rules; FIFA Competition Regulations

attributes.name: sport_code
attributes.description: Standardized sport or discipline code to which this certification applies (e.g., FOOTBALL, BASKETBALL, BASEBALL, HOCKEY, SOCCER, TENNIS, MMA). Enables sport-specific eligibility rule application and cross-sport compliance reporting.
attributes.references: FIFA Regulations; IOC Sport Classification; WADA Prohibited List (sport-specific)

attributes.name: supporting_document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL pointing to supporting documentation stored in the DAM or document management system (e.g., medical certificates, physician letters, venue inspection reports, legal opinions). Enables audit trail linkage without embedding documents in the data product.
attributes.references: WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE); ADA Title III Documentation Requirements; SOX Section 302

attributes.name: wada_adams_tue_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: WADA Anti-Doping Administration and Management System (ADAMS) Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) Reference
attributes.description: Unique reference identifier assigned by the WADA Anti-Doping Administration and Management System (ADAMS) for this Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) record. Enables direct cross-referencing with WADA's global anti-doping database. Null for non-TUE records.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 4.4; WADA ADAMS Platform; WADA International Standard for TUEs (ISTUE)

products.name: arbitration_case
products.description: Unified dispute resolution and case management record for all legal proceedings — CAS (Court of Arbitration for Sport) arbitration, internal arbitration, civil litigation, regulatory investigations, criminal referrals, IP infringement, employment disputes, and CBA grievances. Captures case reference, case type and jurisdiction (sports arbitration vs civil court vs regulatory), claimant/respondent or plaintiff/defendant, filing date, panel or judge composition, external counsel, hearing and trial dates, interim measures, discovery status, estimated liability, award or judgment summary, settlement terms, enforcement status, and matter management reference. Serves as the SSOT for all dispute proceedings regardless of forum.

attributes.name: arbitration_case_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the arbitration or dispute resolution case record within the Sports Entertainment compliance data platform.

attributes.name: requestor_full_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the individual submitting the privacy request. May differ from the fan record name when submitted by an authorized agent or legal representative on behalf of the data subject.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12; CCPA Section 1798.130(a)(3)

attributes.name: response_delivery_method
attributes.description: Method used to deliver the privacy request response or consent confirmation to the data subject. Must align with the data subject's preferred contact channel and regulatory requirements for secure delivery of personal data.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12(1); CCPA Section 1798.130(a)(2)

attributes.name: response_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the privacy request fulfillment. 'fulfilled' = request fully completed; 'partially_fulfilled' = some data categories actioned, others exempted; 'rejected' = request denied with legal basis; 'no_data_found' = no personal data located for the subject; 'extended' = response period extended per regulatory allowance with notice sent.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12(4); CCPA Section 1798.105(b)

attributes.name: submission_channel
attributes.description: Channel through which the data subject submitted the privacy request or provided/withdrew consent. Supports channel analytics and compliance audit trails. Values align with Adobe Experience Platform touchpoint taxonomy.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12; CCPA Section 1798.130(a)

attributes.name: submitted_at
attributes.description: Exact date and time (with timezone) when the privacy request was submitted or the consent event was recorded. This is the principal business event timestamp and the anchor for all regulatory deadline calculations (GDPR 30-day, CCPA 45-day).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12(3); CCPA Section 1798.105(b)

attributes.name: third_party_disclosures
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of third-party organizations to whom the data subject's personal data has been disclosed and who must be notified of erasure, restriction, or opt-out requests. Includes sponsors, broadcast partners, and analytics vendors. Required for GDPR Article 17(2) and CCPA opt-out propagation.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17(2); GDPR Article 19; CCPA Section 1798.120

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Date and time when this privacy request record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change detection for downstream integrations with Adobe Experience Platform and Salesforce CRM.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2); ISO/IEC 27701

attributes.name: us_state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter US state code for data subjects residing in the United States. Used to determine applicability of state-level privacy laws beyond CCPA (e.g., VCDPA for Virginia, CPA for Colorado, CTDPA for Connecticut). Populated only when data_subject_jurisdiction = 'USA'.
attributes.references: CCPA; VCDPA; Colorado Privacy Act; Connecticut Data Privacy Act

attributes.name: verified_at
attributes.description: Date and time when the requestor's identity was successfully verified. Marks the start of the regulatory response clock in jurisdictions where the deadline begins upon verification rather than submission.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 12(3); CCPA Section 1798.105(b)

products.name: data_processing_record
products.description: GDPR Article 30 Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) with integrated Article 35 Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA/PIA) for all personal data processing activities. The authoritative register and risk assessment record capturing processing activity name, controller/processor role, data categories (fan PII, athlete health data, payment data, biometric data), purposes, legal basis, data subjects, retention period, third-party recipients, cross-border transfer mechanisms, security measures, DPIA/PIA assessment type, risk level, identified risks, risk mitigation measures, DPO consultation date, supervisory authority consultation requirement, assessment outcome, approval date, and review schedule. Mandatory for GDPR compliance and required before launching new fan platforms, biometric ticketing, athlete health systems, or any high-risk processing activity.

attributes.name: data_processing_record_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each GDPR Article 30 Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) / Article 35 Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) entry in the compliance register.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30, GDPR Article 35

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: A data processing record (GDPR Article 30 RoPA) is maintained to fulfill a specific compliance obligation. Linking data_processing_record to the obligation it satisfies enables obligation fulfillment

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Data processing activities are owned by specific business units tracked as cost centers. Finance and compliance jointly review processing activities during SOX and privacy audits; cost center attribut
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: processing_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GDPR Article 30 records of processing activities require a named responsible owner. Linking data_processing_record to the employee owner enables DPO oversight, DPIA scheduling, and supervisory authori
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the processing activity and associated DPIA/PIA was formally approved by the authorised approver (e.g., DPO, Chief Privacy Officer, or Legal Counsel). Marks the point from which processing may lawfully commence.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7), ISO 27701

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or role of the individual who formally approved this processing activity record and associated DPIA/PIA (e.g., 'Chief Privacy Officer', 'Data Protection Officer', 'General Counsel'). Provides accountability trail.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2), GDPR Article 35(7)

attributes.name: assessment_outcome
attributes.description: Final outcome of the DPIA/PIA review process. 'Approved' indicates processing may proceed; 'Approved with conditions' requires specific mitigations before go-live; 'Rejected' prohibits processing; 'Not required' indicates no formal assessment was needed.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7), GDPR Article 36

attributes.name: assessment_type
attributes.description: Type of privacy impact assessment conducted for this processing activity. 'dpia' = Data Protection Impact Assessment (mandatory under GDPR Article 35 for high-risk processing); 'pia' = Privacy Impact Assessment (broader scope); 'screening' = pre-DPIA threshold assessment; 'none' = no assessment required.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35, ICO DPIA Guidance

attributes.name: ccpa_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this processing activity is subject to the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) / CPRA, applicable to fan data processing for California residents. Triggers additional consumer rights obligations including opt-out of sale.
attributes.references: CCPA Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100, CPRA

attributes.name: controller_processor_role
attributes.description: Designates whether Sports Entertainment acts as a Data Controller, Data Processor, Joint Controller, or Sub-Processor for this processing activity, as defined under GDPR Article 4. Determines the applicable compliance obligations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4(7), GDPR Article 4(8), GDPR Article 26

attributes.name: cross_border_transfer_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether personal data is transferred to a country outside the European Economic Area (EEA) or to an international organisation. Triggers mandatory documentation of transfer mechanisms under GDPR Chapter V.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 44, GDPR Article 30(1)(e)

attributes.name: data_domain
attributes.description: Business data domain to which this processing activity belongs (e.g., Fan, Athlete, Ticketing). Aligns with Sports Entertainment's enterprise data domain taxonomy for governance and ownership assignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fan|athlete|broadcast|ticketing|sponsorship|finance|workforce|digital_platform|content|venue — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 27701, GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: data_subject_categories
attributes.description: Categories of individuals whose personal data is processed (e.g., 'Fans/Ticket Holders', 'Athletes', 'Employees', 'Minors under 16'). Pipe-delimited list. Mandatory field under GDPR Article 30(1)(c). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fans|athletes|employees|minors|sponsors|media_partners|venue_staff|contractors — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30(1)(c)

attributes.name: dpia_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is mandatory for this processing activity under GDPR Article 35 (e.g., large-scale processing of special category data, systematic monitoring, biometric identification for ticketing).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(1), GDPR Article 35(3)

attributes.name: dpo_consultation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Data Protection Officer (DPO) was formally consulted regarding this processing activity or DPIA. Provides an audit trail for GDPR Article 35(2) compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(2), GDPR Article 38

attributes.name: dpo_consulted
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Data Protection Officer (DPO) was formally consulted during the DPIA/PIA process, as required under GDPR Article 35(2). Mandatory for all high-risk processing activities.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(2), GDPR Article 37-39

attributes.name: identified_risks
attributes.description: Narrative description of privacy risks identified during the DPIA/PIA assessment (e.g., 'Unauthorised access to fan biometric data', 'Re-identification of pseudonymised athlete health records', 'Cross-border transfer of minors' data without adequate safeguards').
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7)(c), ISO 29134

attributes.name: includes_special_category_data
attributes.description: Indicates whether this processing activity involves special category personal data as defined under GDPR Article 9 (e.g., health data, biometric data, racial/ethnic origin). Triggers additional safeguards and explicit consent requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: legal_basis
attributes.description: The lawful basis under GDPR Article 6 (and Article 9 for special category data) that authorises this processing activity. For example, 'consent' for fan marketing, 'contract' for ticketing, 'legal_obligation' for anti-doping compliance under WADA.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6, GDPR Article 9

attributes.name: legitimate_interest_description
attributes.description: Where legal basis is 'legitimate_interests', documents the specific legitimate interest pursued and the balancing test outcome. Required to demonstrate compliance with GDPR Article 6(1)(f) and to evidence the three-part test (purpose, necessity, balancing).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6(1)(f), GDPR Recital 47

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this processing activity record and associated DPIA/PIA. GDPR Article 35(11) requires DPIAs to be reviewed when there is a change in risk. Typically annual for high-risk activities.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(11), ICO RoPA Guidance

attributes.name: pci_dss_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) Applicable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this processing activity involves payment card data and is therefore subject to PCI-DSS requirements. Applicable to ticketing (Ticketmaster/AXS), merchandise (Shopify Plus), and POS transactions at venues.
attributes.references: PCI-DSS v4.0, PCI SSC

attributes.name: personal_data_categories
attributes.description: Categories of personal data processed, including special category data under GDPR Article 9 (e.g., 'Fan PII: name, email, purchase history', 'Athlete health data: injury records, biometrics', 'Payment data: PCI-DSS card data', 'Biometric data: facial recognition for ticketing'). Mandatory under GDPR Article 30(1)(c).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9, GDPR Article 30(1)(c), PCI-DSS v4.0

attributes.name: processing_activity_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the personal data processing activity (e.g., 'Biometric Ticketing Enrollment', 'Fan CRM Profiling', 'Athlete Health Monitoring'). Serves as the primary identity label for the record in the RoPA register.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30(1)(a)

attributes.name: processing_activity_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known unique reference code assigned to this processing activity in the official RoPA register (e.g., 'RoPA-FAN-20240001'). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory filings and supervisory authority correspondence.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30, ISO 27701

attributes.name: processing_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this personal data processing activity ceased or is scheduled to cease. Null for ongoing processing activities. Represents the effective-until date for the processing activity's lifecycle.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30, GDPR Article 5(1)(e)

attributes.name: processing_owner
attributes.description: Business owner responsible for this processing activity (e.g., 'VP Fan Engagement', 'Head of Athlete Performance', 'Director of Ticketing Operations'). Accountable for ensuring ongoing compliance with the documented controls and review schedule.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2), ISO 27701 Section 5.2

attributes.name: processing_purpose
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific purpose(s) for which personal data is processed (e.g., 'Fan personalization and targeted marketing via Adobe Experience Platform', 'Athlete health monitoring for injury prevention'). Must be specific and explicit per GDPR Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation principle.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(b), GDPR Article 13(1)(c)

attributes.name: processing_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which this personal data processing activity commenced or is scheduled to commence. Represents the effective-from date for the processing activity's lifecycle.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30, ISO 27701

attributes.name: processing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the processing activity record within the RoPA register. 'Active' indicates live processing; 'Suspended' indicates temporarily halted; 'Retired' indicates decommissioned processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30, ISO 27701 Section 6.15

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this RoPA/DPIA record was first created in the compliance register. Provides the audit trail creation point for GDPR Article 5(2) accountability principle.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2), ISO 27701

attributes.name: record_last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this RoPA/DPIA record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change management tracking for GDPR Article 30 register maintenance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2), GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: retention_basis
attributes.description: Legal or business justification for the defined retention period (e.g., 'SOX 7-year financial record requirement', 'WADA anti-doping sample retention 10 years', 'PCI-DSS transaction log 1 year', 'GDPR consent withdrawal'). Documents the regulatory driver for the retention schedule.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(e), SOX Section 802, WADA Code Article 17, PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 10.7

attributes.name: retention_period_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of days personal data is retained for this processing activity before deletion or anonymisation, in accordance with GDPR Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation principle. Derived from the applicable retention schedule.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(e), GDPR Article 30(1)(f)

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency for periodic review of this processing activity record and DPIA/PIA. High-risk activities (e.g., biometric ticketing, athlete health systems) typically require annual or biannual review.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(11), ISO 27701 Section 6.15

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Overall residual privacy risk level assigned to this processing activity following DPIA/PIA assessment (e.g., 'high' for biometric ticketing, 'very_high' for athlete health data processing). Determines escalation and supervisory authority consultation requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35, CNIL DPIA Methodology, ISO 29134

attributes.name: risk_mitigation_measures
attributes.description: Specific technical and organisational measures implemented or planned to mitigate identified privacy risks (e.g., 'Biometric data encrypted with hardware security module', 'Athlete health data access restricted to medical staff via SAP SuccessFactors role-based controls', 'DRM applied to broadcast content containing athlete biometrics').
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7)(d), GDPR Article 32, ISO 27001

attributes.name: security_measures
attributes.description: Description of technical and organisational measures implemented to protect personal data (e.g., 'AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, role-based access control, PCI-DSS tokenisation for payment data, pseudonymisation of fan analytics data'). Mandatory under GDPR Article 32 and Article 30(1)(g).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 32, GDPR Article 30(1)(g), PCI-DSS v4.0, ISO 27001

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system of record where the personal data originates or is primarily processed (e.g., 'Salesforce CRM', 'Ticketmaster/AXS', 'Adobe Experience Platform', 'SAP SuccessFactors', 'SportsCode/Hudl'). Enables data lineage tracing for GDPR accountability.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2), ISO 27701 Section 6.12

attributes.name: special_category_data_type
attributes.description: Specific type of special category data processed under GDPR Article 9, where applicable. For Sports Entertainment, common types include 'health' (athlete injury/medical records), 'biometric' (facial recognition ticketing), and 'genetic' (anti-doping testing under WADA). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: health|biometric|genetic|racial_ethnic|religious|political|trade_union|sexual_orientation|criminal_offence|none — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9(1), WADA Code Article 14

attributes.name: supervisory_authority_consultation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the supervisory authority was formally consulted under GDPR Article 36. Null if consultation was not required or has not yet occurred.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36

attributes.name: supervisory_authority_consultation_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Authority Prior Consultation Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether prior consultation with the relevant supervisory authority (e.g., ICO, CNIL) is required before commencing this processing activity, as mandated by GDPR Article 36 when residual risk remains high after mitigation.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36

attributes.name: third_party_recipients
attributes.description: Names and categories of third parties to whom personal data is disclosed (e.g., 'Ticketmaster/AXS — ticketing processor', 'Salesforce CRM — fan relationship management', 'WADA — anti-doping authority', 'Adobe Experience Platform — fan analytics'). Mandatory under GDPR Article 30(1)(d).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30(1)(d), GDPR Article 13(1)(e)

attributes.name: transfer_destination_countries
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes of countries to which personal data is transferred outside the EEA (e.g., 'USA|CAN|AUS'). Pipe-delimited. Required for GDPR Article 30 RoPA documentation and supervisory authority reporting.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30(1)(e), ISO 3166-1

attributes.name: transfer_mechanism
attributes.description: Legal mechanism used to legitimise cross-border personal data transfers where applicable (e.g., 'standard_contractual_clauses' for transfers to US-based Salesforce CRM or Adobe Experience Platform, 'adequacy_decision' for transfers to UK post-Brexit). Mandatory under GDPR Article 46.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 44-49, GDPR Article 30(1)(e)

attributes.name: wada_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this processing activity involves athlete anti-doping data subject to WADA Code requirements, including whereabouts data, biological passport data, and anti-doping test results. Triggers specific data sharing obligations with WADA and national anti-doping organisations.
attributes.references: WADA Code Article 14, WADA International Standard for the Protection of Privacy and Personal Information

attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2) Accountability; SOX; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: data_protection_officer_contact
attributes.description: Contact details (email or phone) of the Data Protection Officer (DPO) for the notifying entity, as required to be disclosed in the notification to the supervisory authority.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(3)(b)

attributes.name: data_protection_officer_name
attributes.description: Name of the Data Protection Officer (DPO) responsible for overseeing the breach notification process and serving as the point of contact with the supervisory authority.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 37 & 33(3)(b)

attributes.name: data_subject_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which affected data subjects were notified of the breach. Required when the breach is likely to result in high risk to individuals under GDPR Article 34.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 34; CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: data_subject_notification_method
attributes.description: Channel used to notify affected data subjects of the breach (e.g., email, postal mail, in-app notification, public notice). Applicable when risk level is high or critical per GDPR Article 34.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 34; CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: gdpr_72hr_deadline_timestamp
attributes.description: Calculated deadline timestamp representing 72 hours after the breach was detected, as mandated by GDPR Article 33(1) for notification to the supervisory authority without undue delay.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(1)

attributes.name: internal_case_reference
attributes.description: Internal legal or compliance case management reference number linking this breach notification to the organisation's internal incident and legal case tracking system.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27035; SOX; GDPR Article 5(2) Accountability

attributes.name: is_supplementary_notification
attributes.description: Indicates whether this notification is a supplementary or updated submission providing additional information to the authority after an initial notification was filed (GDPR Article 33(4) phased notification).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(4)

attributes.name: is_within_72hr_deadline
attributes.description: Indicates whether the notification was submitted within the GDPR-mandated 72-hour window from breach detection. True = compliant; False = late notification requiring documented justification.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(1)

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this breach notification record, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2) Accountability; SOX; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: late_notification_reason
attributes.description: Documented justification for why the notification was submitted after the applicable regulatory deadline (e.g., GDPR 72-hour window). Required by GDPR Article 33(1) when notification is delayed.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(1)

attributes.name: likely_consequences
attributes.description: Description of the probable consequences of the personal data breach for affected individuals, such as identity theft, financial loss, reputational damage, or discrimination. Required under GDPR Article 33(3)(c).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(3)(c)

attributes.name: measures_taken
attributes.description: Description of the technical and organisational measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its adverse effects, as required under GDPR Article 33(3)(d).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(3)(d)

attributes.name: notification_outcome
attributes.description: Final or current outcome of the breach notification as determined by the supervisory authority (e.g., accepted, rejected, investigation opened, further information requested). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: accepted|rejected|under_review|further_info_requested|investigation_opened|closed_no_action — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33 & 58; CCPA

attributes.name: notification_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference code assigned to this notification for tracking with supervisory authorities and internal case management (e.g., BN-2024-000123).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33; CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: notification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the breach notification record, tracking progress from initial drafting through submission, acknowledgment by the authority, and final closure.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33; CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: notification_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the formal breach notification was actually submitted to the supervisory authority or dispatched to affected data subjects.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(1); CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: notification_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this notification is directed to a supervisory authority (e.g., EU Data Protection Authority), to affected data subjects, or both, as required under applicable privacy regulations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33 (supervisory authority) & Article 34 (data subjects); CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: notified_authority_jurisdiction
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which the notified supervisory authority operates (e.g., IRL for Ireland, USA for United States, GBR for United Kingdom).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 55; CCPA; ISO 3166-1

attributes.name: notified_authority_name
attributes.description: Full name of the supervisory authority or regulatory body notified of the breach (e.g., Irish Data Protection Commission, California Attorney General, UK ICO).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33(1); CCPA Section 1798.82

attributes.name: pci_dss_scope_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the breach involves systems or data within the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) cardholder data environment, triggering additional notification obligations to card brands and acquiring banks.
attributes.references: PCI-DSS Requirement 12.10; PCI SSC Incident Response

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary data privacy regulatory framework under which this breach notification obligation arises (e.g., GDPR for EU, CCPA for California). Drives notification timelines and content requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR; CCPA Section 1798.82; LGPD; PIPEDA

attributes.name: regulatory_penalty_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the breach notification circumstances present a risk of regulatory fines or sanctions (e.g., GDPR Article 83 administrative fines up to €20M or 4% of global annual turnover).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 83; CCPA Section 1798.155

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Assessed risk level of the breach to the rights and freedoms of affected data subjects. Determines whether data subject notification is required (high/critical) and the urgency of remediation.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33 & 34; ENISA Guidelines on Personal Data Breach Notification

attributes.name: third_party_processor_involved
attributes.description: Indicates whether a third-party data processor (e.g., ticketing vendor, broadcast partner, merchandise platform) was involved in or contributed to the breach, affecting controller-processor notification obligations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 28 & 33(2); CCPA

attributes.name: third_party_processor_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-party data processor involved in the breach, if applicable. Required for controller accountability and processor notification chain documentation.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 28 & 33(2)

attributes.name: business_unit_owner

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2); ISO/IEC 27001; SOX

attributes.name: data_categories
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of personal data categories involved in the processing activity, e.g., biometric data, health data, financial data, location data, fan behavioral data, athlete performance data. Informs risk classification.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4(1); GDPR Article 9; ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: data_retention_period
attributes.description: Defined retention period for personal data processed under this activity, e.g., '2 years post-event', '7 years for financial records'. Must be justified as part of necessity and proportionality assessment under GDPR Article 5(1)(e).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(e); CCPA; SOX

attributes.name: data_subject_categories
attributes.description: Categories of individuals whose personal data is processed, e.g., fans, athletes, employees, minors, VIP guests, broadcast subscribers. Minors require heightened protection under GDPR Article 8 and COPPA.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4(1); GDPR Article 8; COPPA

attributes.name: data_volume_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated number of data subjects or records affected by the processing activity, e.g., '50,000 fans per event', '500 athletes globally'. Large-scale processing is a key trigger for mandatory DPIA under GDPR Article 35(3)(b).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(3)(b); EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: dpo_advice
attributes.description: Summary of the DPO's formal advice and recommendations provided during consultation, including any conditions or additional safeguards recommended. Must be documented per GDPR Article 35(2).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(2); GDPR Article 38(4)

attributes.name: dpo_consultation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the Data Protection Officer (DPO) was formally consulted regarding this assessment. Required to be documented under GDPR Article 35(2) when DPO consultation is mandatory.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(2); GDPR Article 38

attributes.name: dpo_consultation_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Protection Officer (DPO) Consultation Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether formal consultation with the Data Protection Officer (DPO) is required for this assessment based on risk level and processing nature. Mandatory for high-risk processing under GDPR Article 35(2).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(2); GDPR Article 37-39

attributes.name: identified_risks
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific privacy and data protection risks identified during the assessment, including risks of unauthorized access, data breach, re-identification, discriminatory profiling, and rights violations for data subjects.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7)(c); ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: involves_cross_border_transfer
attributes.description: Indicates whether the processing activity involves transfer of personal data to third countries outside the EEA. Triggers Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) requirements under GDPR Chapter V.
attributes.references: GDPR Chapter V; GDPR Article 46; EDPB Recommendations 01/2020

attributes.name: involves_minors
attributes.description: Indicates whether the processing activity involves personal data of minors (under 16 in EU, under 13 under COPPA). Triggers additional safeguards and parental consent requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 8; COPPA; CCPA

attributes.name: involves_special_category_data
attributes.description: Indicates whether the processing activity involves special category personal data as defined under GDPR Article 9, including biometric data, health data, or genetic data. Triggers mandatory DPIA requirement.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9; GDPR Article 35(3)(b)

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary legal jurisdiction(s) under which the assessment is conducted, e.g., EU (GDPR), USA-CA (CCPA), GBR (UK GDPR). Determines applicable regulatory framework and supervisory authority.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 3; CCPA; UK GDPR

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the PIA/DPIA assessment record. Supports audit trail requirements and tracks assessment lifecycle changes including DPO advice updates and outcome revisions.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(2); ISO/IEC 27001; SOX

attributes.name: lawful_basis
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Lawful Basis
attributes.description: The GDPR Article 6 lawful basis under which the processing activity is conducted. For special category data (e.g., athlete health, biometrics), an Article 9 condition must also be documented in the assessment narrative.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6; GDPR Article 9; CCPA

attributes.name: mitigation_measures
attributes.description: Description of technical and organizational measures proposed or implemented to address identified risks, such as pseudonymization, encryption, access controls, data minimization, consent management, and DRM policies. Required under GDPR Article 35(7)(d).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 25; GDPR Article 32; GDPR Article 35(7)(d); PCI-DSS v4.0

attributes.name: necessity_proportionality_assessment
attributes.description: Documented evaluation of whether the processing is necessary and proportionate to the stated purpose, as required by GDPR Article 35(7)(b). Includes data minimization analysis and retention justification.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(c); GDPR Article 35(7)(b); EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of the PIA/DPIA assessment. GDPR requires reassessment when processing changes materially or at regular intervals. Typically annual for high-risk processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(11); ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: outcome_conditions
attributes.description: Specific conditions, restrictions, or additional safeguards that must be implemented before or during processing when the assessment outcome is 'approved_with_conditions'. Includes implementation deadlines.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35; ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: processing_activity_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative of the data processing activity under assessment, including the nature, scope, context, and purposes of the processing as required by GDPR Article 35(7)(a).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(7)(a); EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: processing_activity_name
attributes.description: Name of the data processing activity being assessed, such as 'Biometric Ticketing System', 'Fan Engagement Personalization Platform', or 'Athlete Health Data Analytics'. Corresponds to the Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) entry.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 30; GDPR Article 35; ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: processing_commenced_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the assessed processing activity commenced operations. Must be on or after the approval date for mandatory DPIAs. Used for compliance audit trail and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35; EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: processing_purpose
attributes.description: The stated business purpose for which personal data is being processed, e.g., fan engagement analytics, athlete health monitoring, biometric access control, or broadcast audience profiling. Required under GDPR Article 35(7)(a).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(b); GDPR Article 35(7)(a)

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary data protection regulatory framework governing this assessment. Determines specific procedural requirements, mandatory consultation thresholds, and documentation obligations.
attributes.references: GDPR; CCPA; UK GDPR; PIPEDA; LGPD; POPIA

attributes.name: residual_risk_level
attributes.description: Residual risk classification after all identified mitigation measures have been applied. If residual risk remains high or very high, supervisory authority consultation is mandatory under GDPR Article 36.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36; ISO/IEC 29134:2017; EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: review_cycle_months
attributes.description: Frequency in months at which the PIA/DPIA must be reviewed and updated, e.g., 12 for annual review, 6 for semi-annual. Determined by risk level and regulatory requirements under GDPR Article 35(11).
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35(11); ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: Overall inherent risk classification of the processing activity prior to mitigation, determined by the assessment team based on data sensitivity, volume, and processing nature. Drives DPO consultation and supervisory authority notification requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35; EDPB Guidelines 09/2022; ISO/IEC 29134:2017

attributes.name: supervisory_authority_consultation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the competent supervisory authority was formally consulted under GDPR Article 36. The authority has up to 8 weeks to respond; processing must be suspended pending response.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36

attributes.name: supervisory_authority_consultation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether prior consultation with the competent supervisory authority (e.g., national Data Protection Authority) is required because residual risk remains high after mitigation, per GDPR Article 36.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36; EDPB Guidelines 09/2022

attributes.name: supervisory_authority_name
attributes.description: Name of the competent data protection supervisory authority consulted or notified, e.g., ICO (UK), CNIL (France), BfDI (Germany), or the lead supervisory authority under GDPR one-stop-shop mechanism.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 36; GDPR Article 56

attributes.name: system_or_platform_name
attributes.description: Name of the information system, platform, or application that performs the processing activity, e.g., Adobe Experience Platform, Ticketmaster Biometric Access, SAP SuccessFactors, or a custom fan engagement platform.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35; PCI-DSS v4.0; ISO/IEC 27001

attributes.name: third_party_processors
attributes.description: Names of external data processors or sub-processors involved in the processing activity, e.g., cloud providers, analytics vendors, ticketing platforms. Relevant for Article 28 processor agreements and transfer impact assessments.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 28; GDPR Article 35(7)(d); CCPA

products.name: accreditation
products.description: This association product represents the formal Accreditation relationship between a governing_body and a vendor. It captures the operational record of a governing body certifying or recognizing a vendor as qualified to operate within a specific regulatory framework or compliance scope. Each record links one governing_body to one vendor and carries accreditation-specific attributes — status, scope, applicable framework, and verification dates — that exist only in the context of this pairing and cannot reside on either the vendor or governing body master record alone.. Existence Justification: In sports entertainment, governing bodies such as WADA, national anti-doping organizations, and league offices formally accredit or certify specific vendors (e.g., anti-doping labs, broadcast technology providers, medical suppliers) to operate within their regulatory frameworks. A single vendor can hold accreditations from multiple governing bodies simultaneously (e.g., a lab accredited by both WADA and a national anti-doping authority), and a single governing body accredits many vendors across its jurisdiction. This is an actively managed operational relationship — compliance teams create, renew, suspend, and audit these accreditations as a core business process.

attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17011, WADA Technical Document TD2021LABC
